hypotheses.justification: Completeness is only needed to lift units from R/I to R. This theorem's right-hand side already assumes IsUnit (coeff 0 f) in R itself, so the lift is not needed. Definition: adicallyRestrictedSubring I = series whose image mod I^k is a polynomial for every k. (→) If f is a unit of the subring, it is a unit in MvPowerSeries σ R, so coeff 0 f is a unit (MvPowerSeries.isUnit_constantCoeff). Also adicReduction I 1 f is a unit in MvPolynomial σ (R/I^1), so by MvPolynomial.isUnit_iff (CommRing only) the coefficients at α ≠ 0 are nilpotent mod I, i.e. lie in I.radical. This is the forward half of isUnit_adicallyRestricted_iff_coeff_mod_ideal, which does not use completeness. (←) Since coeff 0 f is a unit, MvPowerSeries.isUnit_iff_constantCoeff (Mathlib Inverse.lean, any CommRing) gives an inverse g in MvPowerSeries σ R. For each k, the image p of f mod I^k is a polynomial with unit constant coefficient. Its other coefficients are nilpotent in R/I^k: if a^m ∈ I then a^(mk) ∈ I^k. So MvPolynomial.isUnit_iff gives a polynomial inverse q of p. Inverses in MvPowerSeries σ (R/I^k) are unique, so the image of g mod I^k equals q, a polynomial. Hence g is restricted and inverts f in the subring. Degenerate cases (k = 0 with R/⊤ trivial, R trivial, I = ⊤) are harmless. So the iff holds for any CommRing R and ideal I.
